clue.text: Batting so fast is audacious

parts.note: a cricket side that is batting is said to be in
taken as written
Lent is the Christian season of fasting

explanation.surface: A remark that a bowler is batting at a reckless pace.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batting side is 'in'; LENT is the forty-day Christian fast before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Insolent and audacious both describe someone boldly rude and disrespectful.

clue.text: Provisional at home, note, over the Border

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the earlier pieces above the last

parts.note: someone at home is in
te is a note in tonic sol-fa
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: Temporary arrangements made at home and with a note sent across the Scottish Border.
explanation.walkthrough: The Border looks like the England-Scotland frontier, but it is just an edge, RIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim arrangements are temporary, holding until something permanent is settled.

clue.text: What fruitless labour the output of his pen, say

definitions.note: the adjective completes 'What fruitless labour is', describing toil that never ends

indicators.note: the output of suggests these words are produced in a new form, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A writer whose productions are so much wasted effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the output of' rearranges HISPEN and SAY. Sisyphus was condemned to roll a boulder uphill forever.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisyphus in Greek myth pushed a rock uphill eternally, so endless futile toil bears his name.

clue.text: Constant measure of superficial brilliance

explanation.definitionFit: Constant Lambert was an English composer; the lambert is a unit of luminance, how brightly a surface shines.

clue.text: Reserve sum deposited in hope of attracting more

definitions.text: Reserve sum deposited in hope of attracting more

parts.words: Reserve sum deposited in hope of attracting more
parts.note: savings put aside are also read as the dummy egg a poultry keeper leaves in a hen-house to encourage more laying

explanation.definitionFit: Savings put by for the future are named after the dummy egg that tempts a hen to lay.

clue.text: Drink's conveniently placed

parts.note: the apostrophe-s is read as the letter it shows
something handy is close by and easy to reach

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that their drink is within easy reach.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is not a verb but simply supplies an S. A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a common British pub drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A shandy is a pub drink of beer mixed with lemonade or ginger beer.

clue.text: Scoring run, start to improve in status

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the other word

parts.note: one's station in life is one's status
r is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of improve is used

explanation.surface: A batsman's scoring run starts to lift his standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts R and I inside STATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Striation is a pattern of scored lines or grooves.

clue.text: Asked for a very soft piece of music

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft
a lied is a German art song

explanation.surface: Someone requests a quiet musical item.
explanation.walkthrough: PP (pianissimo) is the score marking for very soft; a lied is a German song.
explanation.definitionFit: To have applied is to have made a formal request, as for a job.

clue.text: Exhaust cut-out involves termination of trip

indicators.note: involves means one piece wraps round another

parts.note: to delete is to cut out

indicators.note: termination of means the last letter of trip

explanation.surface: A car exhaust's cut-out device fails at the end of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' puts P, the end of 'trip', inside DELETE.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete a supply is to use it up or drain it.

clue.text: Tax teacher with being a slave-driver

parts.note: to task someone is to tax or burden them, and a task is a duty imposed
a schoolmaster is a teacher, so master works here

explanation.surface: A teacher who levies a tax and behaves like a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A taskmaster is a severe overseer who drives workers hard.

clue.text: He had a game of cards with Joan

definitions.text: He had a game of cards with Joan

parts.words: He had a game of cards with Joan
parts.note: ... Joan is an old card game named after the legendary female pontiff, so the man joined to Joan in its title is the churchman

explanation.walkthrough: Pope Joan is a Victorian card game; the clue reads as a man playing cards with a woman called Joan.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of the Roman Catholic Church shares the card game's name with the legendary Joan.

clue.text: About now Evita changed agent

parts.note: re is a Latin-derived word meaning about or concerning
the present is the time now

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of Evita are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that the musical Evita has been altered recently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns EVITA into ATIVE, which follows RE and PRESENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A representative acts for another person, just as an agent does.

clue.text: Miss West gets back to mining town

parts.note: Mae West was the American film star

indicators.note: back tells us the word gets is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: An actress returns to a town where coal was dug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns GETS into STEG. Maesteg is a former coal-mining town in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Maesteg grew up around coal pits in a Welsh valley, a classic colliery settlement.

clue.text: Taking no account of press story

explanation.definitionFit: Exclusive of means not counting; an exclusive is a news report one paper alone carries.

clue.text: Sifts questions

explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a coarse sieve, so to riddle is to sift; riddles are also puzzling questions.

clue.text: Left everything, being confused with classification

indicators.note: confused tells us the letters are jumbled

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Someone abandons everything, muddled about how things are sorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges ALL and BEING into ABELLING, after L.
explanation.definitionFit: Labelling things is sorting and naming them into categories.

clue.text: Lead pipe?' Lag in advance

indicators.note: in advance means one piece is placed before the other

parts.note: an old lag is a convict, shortened to con
a duct is a pipe or channel

explanation.surface: A question about a lead pipe and how to lag it ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead pipe' looks like plumbing and 'lag' like insulation; in fact 'lag' is a convict (CON), placed 'in advance' of DUCT.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct is to lead or guide, as an orchestra or a tour.

clue.text: Expresses disagreement with aims

explanation.definitionFit: To object is to protest against something; objects are also goals or purposes.

clue.text: Trace record Ernest set out to have erased

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of Ernest are rearranged once the others are gone
to have erased means the letters of set are struck out of Ernest

explanation.surface: A man named Ernest tries to trace a record and wipe it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to have erased' strikes S, E and T out of ERNEST and 'out' rearranges what remains, giving ERN after DISC.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to detect or make out, as one might trace something faint.

clue.text: Ban site replanned lor French resort

indicators.note: replanned says the letters of ban site are laid out afresh

explanation.surface: Developers redesign a site that had been banned for a resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replanned' rearranges BANSITE. Antibes is a town on the French Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibes is a seaside town on the Riviera between Cannes and Nice.

clue.text: Comfort me in a tiny difficulty

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
difficulty suggests the words a tiny are in trouble and so rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking for reassurance while in a small fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficulty' makes ANITY from A TINY, and 'in' puts ME inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An amenity is a facility that adds comfort or convenience.

clue.text: Friendly islanders got up about noon with answer

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round another
in a down clue up means the word got is written from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Sociable islanders rise around midday and reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GOT into TOG, and 'about' puts N inside it. Tonga is known as the Friendly Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga was named the Friendly Islands by Captain Cook, so its people are those islanders.

clue.text: Dubious religious group has got hold of American piano

indicators.note: has got hold of means one piece grips the other inside it

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
p is the musical marking for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A shady sect seizes an American's piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has got hold of' puts US and P inside SECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something suspect is questionable or open to doubt.

clue.text: Israeli general, with son and daughter to rely on, perhaps, turned artist (ned.8).

parts.note: Joshua led the Israelites into Canaan after Moses

indicators.note: turned means these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A biblical commander relies on his children and changes career to painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' rearranges S, D and RELYON into REYNOLDS. Sir Joshua Reynolds was an 18th-century English portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Joshua Reynolds was a leading eighteenth-century portrait painter and first president of the Royal Academy.

clue.text: Each move causes pain

indicators.note: move tells us the letters of each are shifted around

explanation.surface: Every movement hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' rearranges EACH.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a dull continuous pain.

clue.text: Suggestive of mood

explanation.definitionFit: Indicative of means suggestive of; the indicative is the grammatical mood of plain statements.

clue.text: Period of grace of interest to Shylock

explanation.definitionFit: Usance was the customary time allowed for paying a foreign bill; it is also an old word for usury, which Shylock uses in The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Order for troops not to hold river shows vision

indicators.note: not to hold means a letter is left out of the command

parts.note: eyes right is a parade command to soldiers

explanation.surface: A parade command not to keep a river in view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not to hold' takes the R out of EYES RIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing.
